passages.text: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul calls the believers his brothers.
Paul speaks about spiritual gifts.
Paul does not want the believers to be uninformed about spiritual gifts.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν ἀδελφοί οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν

passages.text: You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Christian brothers and sisters in Corinth.
You were once pagans.
You did not know God.
You followed idols.
These idols could not speak.
You let others lead you to these idols.
You were led astray.
passages.original: Οἴδατε ὅτι ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι

passages.text: Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Christian brothers and sisters in Corinth.
Paul wants them to understand spiritual gifts.
Paul says, “I tell you this.”
No one who speaks by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed.”
No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐν Πνεύματι Θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει Αναθεμα ΙΗΣΟΥΣ καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν Κυριος ΙΗΣΟΥΣ εἰ μὴ ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ

passages.text: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.
passages.sermon: There are different gifts.\r\nThe same Spirit gives all these gifts.
passages.original: Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα

passages.text: There are different ministries, but the same Lord.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is the same Lord for all believers.
There are different ministries among believers.
The same Lord, Jesus Christ, is over every ministry.
passages.original: καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς Κύριος

passages.text: There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.
passages.sermon:
God is the one true God.
God works in every person.
There are different ways that God works.
God does all these works Himself.
God works all things in all people.
passages.original: καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς Θεός ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν

passages.text: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
passages.sermon:
God gives the Holy Spirit to each person.
The Spirit shows Himself in each person.
God gives this for the good of everyone.
Each person receives the Spirit’s gift to help all people.
passages.original: Ἑκάστῳ δὲ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ Πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον

passages.text: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit gives gifts to people.
The Spirit gives each person a different gift.
The Spirit gives one person a message of wisdom.
The Spirit gives another person a message of knowledge.
The Spirit gives another person faith.
The Spirit gives another person gifts of healing.
The Spirit gives another person the power to work miracles.
The Spirit gives another person the gift of prophecy.
The Spirit gives another person the ability to tell the difference between spirits.
The Spirit gives another person the ability to speak in different kinds of languages.
The Spirit gives another person the ability to interpret languages.
passages.original: ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ Πνεύματι ἄλλῳ δὲ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ Πνεύματι ἄλλῳ δὲ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων ἄλλῳ δὲ προφητεία ἄλλῳ δὲ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν ἄλλῳ δὲ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν

passages.text: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit is one.
The Holy Spirit is the same for all believers.
The Holy Spirit works all these gifts.
The Holy Spirit gives each person a gift.
The Holy Spirit decides which gift each person receives.
passages.original: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται

passages.text: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.
passages.sermon:
A body is one whole thing.
A body has many parts.
All the parts together make one body.
Christ is like this body.
Christ is one.
Christ has many members.
All the members together are one in Christ.
passages.original: Καθάπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ἕν ἐστιν καὶ μέλη πολλὰ ἔχει πάντα δὲ τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώματος πολλὰ ὄντα ἕν ἐστιν σῶμα οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit is one.
The Holy Spirit acts with unity.
The Holy Spirit brings all believers together.
We all received baptism by the Holy Spirit.
We all became part of one body through this Spirit.
This is true for every believer.
Some of us are Jews.
Some of us are Greeks.
Some of us are slaves.
Some of us are free people.
No matter who we are, we all share in the same Spirit.
The Holy Spirit was given to all of us.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ Πνεύματι ἡμεῖς πάντες εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἴτε Ἰουδαῖοι εἴτε Ἕλληνες εἴτε δοῦλοι εἴτε ἐλεύθεροι καὶ πάντες ἓν Πνεῦμα ἐποτίσθημεν

passages.text: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.
passages.sermon:
The body has many parts.
The body does not have only one part.
Each part is different.
All the parts together make up the body.
passages.original: Καὶ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα οὐκ ἔστιν ἓν μέλος ἀλλὰ πολλά

passages.text: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
passages.sermon:
The body has many different parts.
The foot is one part of the body.
The hand is another part of the body.
The foot might say, "I am not a hand."
The foot might also say, "I do not belong to the body."
But the foot is still part of the body.
Not being a hand does not remove the foot from the body.
passages.original: ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὁ πούς Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ χείρ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος

passages.text: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
passages.sermon:
The ear is a part of the body.
The ear is different from the eye.
The ear might say, "I am not an eye."
The ear might say, "I do not belong to the body."
This statement does not change the truth.
The ear still belongs to the body.
The ear is still a part of the body.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν εἴπῃ τὸ οὖς Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὀφθαλμός οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος

passages.text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
passages.sermon:
A body has many parts.
Each part has a special purpose.
If the whole body were only an eye, the body could not hear.
If the whole body were only an ear, the body could not smell.
passages.original: εἰ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ὀφθαλμός ποῦ ἡ ἀκοή εἰ ὅλον ἀκοή ποῦ ἡ ὄσφρησις

passages.text: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.
passages.sermon:
God created the human body.
God placed each part in the body.
God decided where every part should be.
God arranged every part as He wanted.
Each part is in its place because of God’s plan.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἔθετο τὰ μέλη ἓν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ σώματι καθὼς ἠθέλησεν

passages.text: If they were all one part, where would the body be?
passages.sermon: A body has many parts.\r\nIf every part were the same part, the body would not exist.\r\nIf all were one part, there would be no body.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἦν τὰ πάντα ἓν μέλος ποῦ τὸ σῶμα

passages.text: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
passages.sermon:
God created the body.
The body has many parts.
The body is still one body.
Each part is different.
All parts belong to the same body.
passages.original: νῦν δὲ πολλὰ μὲν μέλη ἓν δὲ σῶμα

passages.text: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”
passages.sermon:
The human body has many different parts.
Each part is important.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I do not need you."
The head cannot say to the feet, "I do not need you."
Every part needs the other parts.
passages.original: Οὐ δύναται δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί Χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω ἢ πάλιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῖς ποσίν Χρείαν ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔχω

passages.text: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty, whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it, so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.
passages.sermon:
Some parts of the body seem weaker.
These parts are actually necessary.
Some parts of the body seem less honorable.
We give these parts greater honor.
Some parts of the body are unpresentable.
We treat these parts with special modesty.
Some parts of the body are presentable.
These presentable parts do not need special treatment.
God put the body together.
God gave more honor to the parts that lacked it.
God did this so the body would not be divided.
God wants all the members to care for each other.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὰ δοκοῦντα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενέστερα ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖά ἐστιν καὶ ἃ δοκοῦμεν ἀτιμότερα εἶναι τοῦ σώματος τούτοις τιμὴν περισσοτέραν περιτίθεμεν καὶ τὰ ἀσχήμονα ἡμῶν εὐσχημοσύνην περισσοτέραν ἔχει τὰ δὲ εὐσχήμονα ἡμῶν οὐ χρείαν ἔχει Ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς συνεκέρασεν τὸ σῶμα τῷ ὑστερουμένῳ περισσοτέραν δοὺς τιμήν ἵνα μὴ ᾖ σχίσμα ἐν τῷ σώματι ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσιν τὰ μέλη

passages.text: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.
passages.sermon:
The body of Christ is made up of many members.
Each person is a member of this body.
If one member suffers, all members suffer together.
If one member is honored, all members rejoice together.
passages.original: καὶ εἴτε πάσχει ἓν μέλος συμπάσχει πάντα τὰ μέλη εἴτε δοξάζεται ἓν μέλος συνχαίρει πάντα τὰ μέλη

passages.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.
passages.sermon:
You are the body of Christ.
Each of you is a member of this body.
Christ joins you together as one body.
God gives each person a place in this body.
Each member belongs to the whole body.
Each member has a part to play.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε σῶμα Χριστοῦ καὶ μέλη ἐκ μέρους

passages.text: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.
passages.sermon:
God appoints people in the church.
He gives each person a role.
First, God appoints apostles.
Second, God appoints prophets.
Third, God appoints teachers.
Then, God appoints those who work miracles.
God also appoints people with gifts of healing.
He appoints people who help others.
He appoints people who lead and guide.
He appoints people who speak different kinds of tongues.
passages.original: Καὶ οὓς μὲν ἔθετο ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρῶτον ἀποστόλους δεύτερον προφήτας τρίτον διδασκάλους ἔπειτα δυνάμεις ἔπειτα χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἀντιλήμψεις κυβερνήσεις γένη γλωσσῶν

passages.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
passages.sermon:
Not everyone is an apostle.
Not everyone is a prophet.
Not everyone is a teacher.
Not everyone works miracles.
passages.original: μὴ πάντες ἀπόστολοι μὴ πάντες προφῆται μὴ πάντες διδάσκαλοι μὴ πάντες δυνάμεις

passages.text: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
passages.sermon: Not everyone has gifts of healing.\r\nNot everyone speaks in tongues.\r\nNot everyone interprets tongues.
passages.original: μὴ πάντες χαρίσματα ἔχουσιν ἰαμάτων μὴ πάντες γλώσσαις λαλοῦσιν μὴ πάντες διερμηνεύουσιν

passages.text: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He tells them to desire the greater spiritual gifts.
He says, “Eagerly desire the greater gifts.”
He also says, “Now I will show you the most excellent way.”
passages.original: ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα Καὶ ἔτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ὁδὸν ὑμῖν δείκνυμι
